district.description: Located in the central part of Tamil Nadu, Perambalur is an agrarian district rich in paleontology—famous for its ancient marine fossils and the historic Ranjankudi Fort.

culturalEntries.title: Ranjankudi Fort
culturalEntries.shortDescription: A 17th-century fortress built by the Jagirdar of the Nawab of Carnatic, showcasing exquisite Islamic military architecture.
culturalEntries.fullDescription: Built in the 17th century by a Jagirdar under the Nawab of Carnatic, Ranjankudi Fort is a remarkable example of Islamic military architecture in Tamil Nadu. The fort features three defensive tiers—a lower tier, a middle tier, and the citadel—constructed with cut stone blocks. It includes semi-circular bastions, a moat, a palace area, underground chambers, and a mosque. The fort was the site of the pivotal Battle of Valikondah in 1751 during the Carnatic Wars between the British and the French.
culturalEntries.historyOrigin: Constructed in the 17th century during the rule of the Nawabs of Carnatic.
culturalEntries.culturalSignificance: A crucial military monument that played a significant role in the Second Carnatic War, illustrating the era's sophisticated defensive architecture and water management systems.
culturalEntries.sourceReferences: State Archaeological and Historical Documentation; Tamil Nadu Tourism

chatbotKnowledge.answerEn: The Ranjankudi Fort in Perambalur district is a 17th-century fortress built by the Nawabs of Carnatic. It is famous for its three-tiered defensive architecture and its historical role in the Carnatic Wars of 1751.
chatbotKnowledge.answerTa: பெரம்பலூர் மாவட்டத்தில் உள்ள ரஞ்சன்குடி கோட்டை 17-ஆம் நூற்றாண்டில் கர்நாடக நவாப்களால் கட்டப்பட்டது. இது மூன்று அடுக்கு பாதுகாப்பு கட்டமைப்புகளையும், 1751 கர்நாடகப் போரில் முக்கியப் பங்காற்றிய வரலாற்றையும் கொண்டது.
